text:
Emmitt Finnie was the 201st pick in 2023, and at 21 he is playing nearly 20 minutes a night for the Red Wings, more lately than earlier in the season. Seven goals in 21 games already looks like a seventh-round steal, and by NHL EDGE tracking his 104 bursts over 20 mph rank him at the top of the league.

He's also in a rut: no points in six straight games. But the chances haven't gone anywhere. He had 3.5 expected goals in that stretch (a measure of chance quality), and Detroit gets 57% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice, almost ten points better than without him. That's a strong mark on a team that has struggled since Dylan Larkin stopped playing.

His shooting (15.6%) sits a bit above our range for him, so this isn't a player due for a flood of goals. What we'd expect is points to return in step with the chances. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting 1.5 shots per 60 off the best passes in the game, across the slot or from behind the net. Watch who's feeding him.
